The resolution urges condemnation of violence and hate speech motivated by discrimination, consistent with international law, while encouraging civil society participation and dialogue.

The Council requests monitoring and regular reporting from UN peacekeeping and special political missions under existing mandates. It requests a public oral briefing from the Secretary-General by 14 June 2024 and swift alerts on related threats. The text does not create a censorship power.

On 14 June 2023, the Council unanimously adopted UAE and UK draft S/2023/427 as resolution 2686 (2023), with 15 votes in favour. The resolution urges condemnation of violence and hate speech motivated by discrimination, consistent with international law, while encouraging civil society dialogue.

France objected to religious discussions in the Council, insisting freedom of expression be respected and warning against a broad view of extremism.
